action_summary: Add the second closed goal contract to the world broker: env-ready, and close the bottleneck round 1 named. The broker could already answer run-tests, but every real repository it met needed an environment it did not have, and the refusal that followed was about the environment, not the task. env-ready demands: every dependency the environment declares is present, at a spec-satisfying version, in the isolated interpreter that environment will be asked in, and provable by execution. Host-first: anything the isolation already has costs a metadata read and an import, never a round trip. Otherwise the artifact comes from the machine-readable registry (pypi.org JSON), is hashed by us and compared against the registry's own published digest (two independent readers), installed from local bytes, and read back by import -- not just by version. Transitives are resolved from each verified wheel's own METADATA, marker-filtered, including the project's own extras, which is how requests' SOCKS tests pass. ROUND 2 changed what counts as a declaration: the reader is now stdlib tomllib throughout (a single quote inside a double-quoted requirement desynchronised the regex reader on tox), and it understands four shapes that five unseen repositories actually use -- extras installed by the project's own test environment (black's `.[d]`, 800 passed), dependency-groups with {include-group} (attrs), markers with inner quoted comparisons (tox), and extras declared as DATA in tox.toml (`extras = [ "completion" ]`, which is why tox's suite can import argcomplete and run 4253 tests instead of failing to collect). A plugin is armed by its host (PLUGIN_ARMED_IMPORTED_BY_HOST, deferred import) and the final gate now exempts exactly those records, so a plugin is not refused for the import its host owns. A suite may be run by the project's own declared command, not just `-m pytest`, and the isolation is the only thing asked. ROUND 2 also fixed the broker's worst honesty defect: it reported refusals ABOUT THE ENVIRONMENT for facts about THE PROJECT. attrs (1408 passed, one genuine py3.11 upstream failure) and tox (4253 passed, three errors from a missing system binary `man`) were both reported as REFUSE__NO_RUNNER_EXECUTED_CLEANLY. REFUSE__VERIFICATION_FAILED now means the suite RAN in the armed environment and did not exit cleanly; NO_RUNNER_EXECUTED_CLEANLY means nothing ran. A timeout is reported as a bound of ours, not as a verdict about either. The project installs itself from a staged copy so the tree is never written into, and .git is kept because hatch-vcs/setuptools-scm BUILD the version from history (measured: without tags tox cannot import its own generated tox/version.py). History therefore enters the evidence digest, so an environment armed without tags is a different environment and is re-derived rather than answered from a stale record. Memory is keyed by the evidence digest and never believed: a warm run re-reads every version and re-imports every module, and a tampered record is caught and re-derived.

falsification_condition: Falsified if any warm arm returns a version or import state the interpreter contradicts, if any artifact's bytes disagree with the registry's published digest and installation proceeds anyway, or if a repository whose suite passes after arming shows a declared dependency absent. All three are tested; the live tamper case is the standing control.
highest_leverage_note: Two closed contracts either side of a real task now exist in one broker. The next leverage is the same contract shape where the guide is not a manifest at all -- GUI/DOM -- which is blocked in this sandbox (no display) and must be measured elsewhere, not claimed.
honest_limits: Producer-run sandbox only. No independent verifier has reproduced any number here; truth.achieved stays false.

Two of five suites do not exit cleanly, and both are reported as such, not smoothed over: attrs has a genuine upstream failure on Python 3.11, and tox's man-page tests shell out to the system binary `man`, which this sandbox does not have. Neither is offered as a capability.

System binaries are not declarations. `man`, `node`, `gcc` are required by real suites and stated in no manifest; env-ready learns of them only by watching a suite fail. That tier is named as the next step, not built.
GUI/DOM arming remains blocked: no display in this sandbox.
A warm answer is re-executed, never believed, so the warm path is fast but not free: it still runs the project's own test command.
load_bearing_note: The success probability is a producer estimate for the measurement succeeding (it did), not for any frontier benchmark score moving.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: No open obligation is discharged by this producer-run measurement, and none is claimed to be. The causal path is constructive: Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks of any size arrive as repositories whose environments must be armed before any suite can be asked, and the broker's inability to arm one was the standing wall in front of every one of them. That wall now has a measured, refusal-named solution on two unseen repositories. The unlock is stated as 1/66 -- one task's worth of an envelope -- because arming is a precondition for the benchmark, not a score on it.

next_step: Close the gap this round measured: system binaries are not declarations. tox's own suite fails with FileNotFoundError: 'man', and no pyproject.toml states it. Build the declared-by-observation tier for executables -- derive the requirement from the suite's own evidence (subprocess targets, its CI workflow, its docs build), then verify it by execution (which + --version) exactly as imports are verified now, and report it as a third refusal vocabulary item rather than as a project failure. This is the same contract shape as GUI/DOM arming with the evidence source moved from manifest to observation; GUI/DOM itself stays blocked (no display in this sandbox).
real_outcome: An environment the system has never seen is now armed from the environment's own declarations with two-reader digest agreement, proven by execution, remembered by evidence, and re-checked on every reuse -- and the other goal can then be asked in it.
